recipe.name: Pan-Sized Perfection: The Ultimate Scallion Pancakes | 「與鍋同大」的完美蔥油餅 （葱油饼 cōng yóu bǐng）
recipe.description: Scallion pancakes use simple ingredients and are quick to make, but shaping them perfectly can be tricky. 蔥油餅配料簡單、省時好做，但總是擀不好形狀。 This recipe shares a detailed guide alongside one core technique: how to effortlessly craft a "perfectly sized" scallion pancake with clean, round edges that completely fits your skillet. 这个菜譜不僅分享詳細流程，更要解鎖一個核心技巧：怎樣輕鬆做出鋪滿鍋底、邊緣圓整的「完美尺寸」蔥油餅。 Prepare the dough disk on Day 1 and chill overnight, then pan-fry it fresh for breakfast on Day 2. 第一天預製餅胚冷藏，第二天煎制當早餐。
recipe.keywords: crispy pancakes, scallion recipe, homemade snack

recipeInstructions.text:
DAY 1
Knead Dough: Dissolve the starter discard in water (reserve ~15ml to adjust later). Add flour, salt, and oil. Knead until no dry flour remains. Rest for 20 minutes.

和面： 老面加入水攪散（留約15毫升水，後加）；加入中筋粉、鹽、油；揉至沒有干粉；靜置20分鐘。

Make the Roux: Combine oil, flour, salt, and thirteen-spice powder. Stir until smooth.

做油酥： 食用油、中筋粉、鹽、十三香；攪拌均勻。

Divide & Roll: Divide the dough into 8 equal portions. Roll each piece thin into a circle.

分割與擀薄： 面團分為8份，擀薄呈圓形。

Layer Pastes & Scallions: Spread roux and scatter chopped scallions as evenly as possible over the surface.

抹油酥、撒蔥花： 盡量均勻鋪開。

Roll into Cones: Cut a single slit from the center to the outer edge. Roll the dough around the center point into a cone shape. Pinch edges to seal and press down top-to-bottom to form a disk.

卷餅胚： 從圓心處往邊割斷面皮；以圓心為頂點卷起，呈圓錐狀；開口收口，按壓錐尖成餅胚。

Chill: Spray/lightly coat each disk with oil, wrap tightly in plastic film, and store in the refrigerator overnight.

冷藏： 保鮮膜噴少許食用油裹住餅胚入冰箱冷藏。

DAY 2
Preheat & Oil: Preheat a cast-iron skillet. Turn heat to medium-low, add cooking oil, then lay down the pancake disk.

熱鍋冷油： 預熱鑄鐵鍋；轉中小火後倒油；下餅胚。

Flatten to Fit: Lightly spray oil on the pancake's surface, cover with parchment paper, and press down firmly using a second flat skillet until it forms a uniform circle filling the pan.

壓制餅胚： 餅胚表面噴少許食用油；蓋上烘焙紙；用另一個平底鍋下壓，使餅胚呈完美的圓形。

Pan-Fry: Fry for 1–2 minutes per side first, then flip and cook for another 30–60 seconds per side until golden. Let cool briefly before serving.

煎制： 每面先煎1-2分鐘；再每面煎半分鐘到1分鐘；出鍋後冷卻片刻即可食用。

recipe.howToTip:
TIPS & SUBSTITUTIONS | 小貼士与替代方案:

The ratio of sourdough discard to all-purpose flour can be adjusted based on the amount of starter you need to use up.
老面與中筋面粉的比例可以根據手頭的拋棄面糊量自由調整。

If you don't have starter discard, blend flour and water at a 1:1 ratio. For instance, 50g flour + 50g water + 2g active dry yeast seamlessly replaces 100g of starter.
沒有老面，按一比一的比例將面粉和水混合。如，粉水各50克加入2克干酵母，可以替代100克老面。
recipeIngredient: 300 g Sourdough Starter Discard (1:1 hydration)| 老面（粉水1:1）
50 g Cooking Oil (Lard works best) | 食用油（豬油最佳）
120 g Chopped Scallions (The more the merrier; wash, thoroughly drain, and slice) | 越多越好，洗淨後瀝干水分再切

recipe.name: The Ultimate Low-Sugar Banana Pancakes
recipe.description: Thick, soft, and extra-fluffy! Made with two whole ripe bananas and just a hint of added sugar, these pancakes are naturally sweet, perfectly golden, and practically made for a drizzle of honey. I'm tweaking the recipe to get the fluffiness just right—give them a try this weekend and let me know how yours turned out in the comments! This recipe is for 2 servings ( 4 to 5 pancakes)
recipe.keywords: low sugar pancakes, healthy breakfast, quick banana recipe

recipeInstructions.text: Whisk dry ingredients: In a bowl, combine the flour, ½ tbsp sugar, 1 tsp baking powder, 1/4 teaspoon baking soda, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1/4 tsp ground cinnamon.
Mix wet ingredients: In a separate bowl, thoroughly mash both bananas until smooth. Whisk in the egg, milk, melted butter, and vanilla.
Fold gently (Key step for fluffiness): Pour wet into dry. Fold with a spatula just until the flour disappears. Stop immediately—lumps are expected and essential.

Preheat electric stove & rest batter: Set your electric burner to 3 (Medium-Low, on a 1–10 dial) and let your skillet heat up for 3–5 minutes. Let the batter rest undisturbed for 5 minutes during this time.

Cook: Heat a non-stick skillet over medium-low heat and grease lightly. Scoop ⅓ cup of batter per pancake. Cook 2–3 minutes until bubbles form on top, flip gently, and cook 1–2 minutes until golden. (Never press down on the pancakes with your spatula!). (If the outsides brown too quickly before the center cooks, lower the dial to 2.5).
Topping Instructions
1. Stack & Dust: Stack warm pancakes. Dust lightly with powdered sugar (optional, skip for diabetic friendly).
2. Add Fruit: Top with fresh strawberries, blueberries, and raspberries.
3. Drizzle: Finish with a drizzle of honey (skip or substitute with zero-sugar syrup for diabetics).

recipe.name: California Farm Soy Natto Paste for Miso Soup
recipe.description: Natto smells and tastes like overripe Camembert cheese. Four plastic 1 pound tubs of this fermented soy bean paste are enough for a years supply of Miso soup and miso breakfast snack for two people. Here is the recipe that works for us year after year.
recipe.keywords: fermented soy paste, homemade miso, traditional natto

recipeInstructions.text: Soak 2 pounds of whole soy beans in 4 parts of water 12 hours till bubbles appear on top of the water. Makes 4 pounds. Whisk beans on slow in bread maker to remove loosened hulls. Rinse and drain.

Boil dehulled beans in 2 parts water for 6 hours till soft. Add water every hour to keep beans immersed. After adding water, stir, skim foam and floating hulls off the top. The beans are done when they turn to puree pressed between thumb and finger. Drain. Puree in 2 cup increments in foodprocessor with Tbs old natto and 1/4 cup water till smooth.

Ladle into glass baking dish, make a 2” layer. Cover with shrinkwrap. Put in oven with oven light on, top shelf is usally 110F-120F degrees, bottom shelf is 100F degrees, put mash at 100F to 120F degrees. Taste every six hours. When you like the taste, Cool in fridge to stop fermentation. Done! Freeze three tubs, use one, keep well sealed.

recipeIngredient: 2 pounds dry non GMO whole soybeans

recipe.name: Japanese Grilled Eggplant - Yaki Nasu
recipe.description: Japanese grilled eggplant, or yaki nasu, is a quick and easy Japanese recipe. It can be easily prepared in less than 30 minutes. Since Japanese recipes focus on retaining the natural flavor of the ingredients, not much heavy seasonings and sauces are used. For this particular recipe, grilled eggplants are simply served with grated ginger, katsuobushi and soy sauce. If you want to make it gluten free, just make sure to use gluten-free soy sauce instead. I use Japanese or Chinese eggplants for this recipe; these eggplants are longer and slimmer in shape. (My instruction video: https://youtu.be/fmTeXyskjwo)

recipe.name: Spicy Cold Tofu Skin Salad (Liángbàn Dòufupí - 拌豆腐皮)
recipe.description: A refreshing Asian-style cold salad made of shredded tofu sheets and crunchy julienned vegetables, tossed in a traditional, vibrant Málà dressing. This dish features a homemade chili oil infused with Sichuan peppercorns and dried chilies, perfectly balancing heat, tingly citrus notes, and crisp freshness. Perfect for a light summer meal! #HotDaysCoolIdeas #MySummerCooking
recipe.keywords: spicy salad, tofu skin recipe, easy Asian appetizer

recipeInstructions.text: Hydrate the Mushrooms: Place the dried wood ear mushrooms in a bowl of boiling water. Let them soak for at least 15 minutes until plump and soft.

Prep the Tofu: Slice the tofu sheets into thin, noodle-like strips. Bring a pot of water to a boil, blanch the tofu strips for 2 minutes, then immediately plunge them into a bowl of ice water to stop the cooking. Drain well and set aside.

Chop the Vegetables: Cut the cilantro (including the tender stems) into 2-inch (5 cm) pieces. Julienne the carrots and cucumber. Drain the rehydrated mushrooms, trim off any tough, woody stems, and slice them into bite-sized pieces.
Prep the Chiles: Cut the dried chiles into 3/4-inch (2 cm) pieces. Soak them in a small bowl of water for a few minutes to prevent burning, then drain thoroughly.
Prep Aromatics: Thinly slice the white parts of the scallions and the red onion lengthwise into julienne strips. Finely mince the garlic and place it into a medium, heatproof bowl.

Infuse the Oil: Heat a wok or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the canola oil. If using raw canola oil, heat it until it just starts to smoke, then lower the heat. Carefully add the drained dried chiles and the Sichuan peppercorns.

Sizzle: Stir-fry the spices continuously with a spatula for about 30 seconds until fragrant. Immediately remove the wok from the heat and carefully pour the hot, infused oil over the minced garlic in the heatproof bowl. It will sizzle beautifully.

Finish the Dressing: Add the Chinkiang black vinegar, dark soy sauce, toasted sesame oil, sesame seeds, sugar, and MSG to the garlic-oil mixture. Whisk well. Taste the dressing—you can balance the tartness by adding a pinch of sugar or vinegar, to taste.

Assemble the Salad: In a large mixing bowl, combine the drained tofu strips, carrots, cucumber, wood ear mushrooms, red onion, and scallions. Pour the dressing over the ingredients and toss thoroughly to coat everything evenly. Fold in the fresh cilantro.

Garnish and Serve: Let the salad sit for a few minutes to let the flavors develop. Portion onto plates and garnish with extra crushed Sichuan peppercorns and the green tops of the scallions sliced into rings.

recipe.howToTip: Chop the Vegetables: Cut the cilantro (including the tender stems) into 2-inch (5 cm) pieces. Julienne the carrots and cucumber. Drain the rehydrated mushrooms, trim off any tough, woody stems, and slice them into bite-sized pieces.

recipe.name: Traditional Mapo Tofu plant-based (Chuántǒng Sù Mápó Dòufu 传统素麻婆豆腐)
recipe.description: This dish is a vibrant, plant-based adaptation of the iconic Sichuan classic. While traditional Mapo Tofu relies on minced pork or beef to add texture and depth, this recipe masterfully substitutes animal protein without losing the dish's soul. By using a clever combination of finely minced king oyster mushrooms and chopped walnuts (or high-quality soy/pea granules), we perfectly replicate the rich, savory, and slightly crispy mouthfeel of traditional minced meat.The heart of the dish remains untouched: the intense, umami-rich foundation of fermented Pixian Doubanjiang, the punchy kick of black beans, and the signature málà (spicy and numbing) sensation delivered by the fresh knife-chopped Sichuan peppercorns and chilies. It is a deeply satisfying, fiery, and aromatic experience that proves you don’t need meat to honor a time-tested culinary tradition.
recipe.keywords: Chao tian chilies (medium heat Sichuan Facing Heaven, Chao Tian Jiao 朝天椒),Green Sichuan peppercorns. Red Sichuan peppercorns as an alternative (Qīnghuājiāo 青花椒),Vegetable oil,King oyster mushrooms and walnuts,soy/pea granules,plant-based ground meat,Organic medium-soft tofu,For the Mapo Tofu,Rapeseed oil OR a different seed oil like Avocado,Deodorized coconut oil - optional used to simulate the traditional rich fat content of meat,Pixian Doubanjiang or Cantonese doubanjiang like Lee Kum Kee as an alternative (Pixian Doubanjiang 郫县豆瓣酱),Roughly chopped fermented black beans (Dòuchǐ 豆豉),Ginger finely diced,Garlic clove, finely diced,water or vegetable broth,Corn starch,Small scallions (green onions), sliced into thin rings,Sugar,Msg,water (for cornstarch slurry)

recipeInstructions.text:
Blanch the tofu: 

Pour one liter of water and a teaspoon of salt into the wok, then bring to a boil. In the meantime, cut the tofu into roughly 2 cm cubes. When the water starts to boil, gently slide the tofu cubes in and let them simmer for 2 minutes.

Prepare the knife-chopped chili mixture: 

Cut all the Chao Tian chilies into 3 or 4 slices with scissors, discarding the seeds to reduce the heat, then place them in a small bowl with the Sichuan peppercorns.

Heat your wok, add the seed oil, and bring it to 130°C. Then add the chili slices and Sichuan peppercorns, toasting them for about 30 seconds.
Put out the heat and transfer to a cutting board, crush with a Chinese cleaver/knife, finely chop, and set aside.

Meat substitutes and other ingredients:

When using King Oyster mushrooms and walnuts, finely mince the mushrooms and chop the walnuts with a knife to achieve a texture similar to minced meat. 
If you are using soy or pea granules, rehydrate them according to the package instructions and thoroughly squeeze out any excess water.
Finely mince the garlic and the ginger and set aside. Finally, cut the spring onions on small rounds and if you like, some cilantro, that will be used for the garnish.

Cook the sauce and tofu:

Dry the wok and heat it over medium heat. Add rapeseed oil, then, once hot, add your preferred plant-based meat (such as mushrooms and walnuts, granules, or store-bought mince) along with deodorized coconut oil. Stir-fry until the mixture becomes golden brown and slightly crispy.

Turn the heat down to low, then add the Doubanjiang and the fermented black beans (Dòuchǐ) and Fry gently for about 1 to 2 minutes, stirring constantly, until the oil turns a deep, bright red and releases its rich aroma.
Toss in the diced ginger and garlic. Stir-fry over medium heat for another 30 seconds until fragrant, being careful not to burn them. Add 2/3 of the traditional knife-chopped chili and stir well

Pour the water or vegetable broth into the wok and bring to a boil. Add the salt, sugar and MSG.
Gently drain the tofu from the warm water and add it to the wok. Carefully push the tofu with the back of your Chinese ladle (moving from the edges toward the center in smooth motions) to avoid breaking it, then let it simmer over medium-low heat for about 5 minutes so it absorbs all the sauce's flavors.

Thicken and Finish: 

Give the cornstarch-and-water mixture (the slurry) a quick stir. Pour one-third of it into the wok in a thin stream while gently moving the tofu, and let it thicken for a few seconds.

Add the second third of the slurry and let it simmer briefly, then add the remaining slurry, turning off the heat. This multi-step process allows the sauce to bind perfectly without forming clumps and softens your tofu; this makes the sauce thick, glossy, and completely coats the tofu cubes.

Turn off the heat and transfer the Mapo Tofu into a large serving dish or deep bowl. Generously dust the top with the remaining knife-chopped chili-and-Sichuan-pepper mixture and scallions / cilantro you prepared earlier.

recipe.howToTip: I Peperoncini Chao Tian offrono un livello di piccantezza medio e sono utilizzati principalmente per il loro aroma. Quando li sostituisci con altri Peperoncini, regola la quantità in base al loro grado di piccantezza. Per questa ricetta si consiglia l'Olio di Colza, poiché il suo sapore esalta la profondità del piatto.

recipeInstructions.text: Cook the tofu: Add 1½ tablespoons oil to a large nonstick frying pan and heat on medium-high for 2 minutes. Add half of the tofu, arranging it with as little overlap as possible. Cook undisturbed until deeply golden brown and crispy on the bottom, occasionally shaking the pan to encourage even browning, 4 to 5 minutes.

Use a wide spatula to flip the tofu (some pieces will stick together, that’s fine) and cook until deeply golden brown on the second side, 2 to 3 minutes. Transfer the tofu to a wire rack. Add the remaining oil to the pan. Once it’s shimmering, add the remaining tofu. Cook as above, keeping in mind that the second batch may cook a bit faster.

When the second batch is done, reduce the heat to low and return the first batch of tofu to the pan with the second batch. Sprinkle the shawarma spice blend over all of the tofu. Use a silicone spatula to toss the tofu in the spices, stirring constantly for 30 seconds. Transfer all of the tofu to the wire rack to further crisp up. Season with a pinch of salt, as needed.

While the tofu cooks, make the tahini sauce: In a medium bowl, combine the tahini, ice water, lemon juice, sugar, ½ teaspoon kosher salt and several twists of pepper. Whisk until pourable but creamy, adding more ice water as needed. Season with sugar for sweetness, lemon juice for acidity, or salt as needed.

To serve, divide warm rice among four bowls. Top with tofu shawarma and sliced vegetables. Spoon a bit of the onion-pickling liquid on top of the rice and vegetables. Add the sumac onions and dollop the tahini sauce on top. Before serving, tear the mint leaves with your hands over the bowls.

Throw it in the blender if you want the meat to be fine. The key is to taste everything as you go, and modify to your liking.
recipe.keywords: hearty dinner, layered pasta, homemade Italian

recipeInstructions.text: Start getting a large pot of water up to near-boiling for pasta.
Small dice onion, poblano peppers, and mince garlic.

Brown the sausage in a 12" skillet, while breaking it up.
Then add diced/minced veggies, and cook until softened.

Add 1 jar of sauce. Save the other 1/2 for plating later.

Season to taste (salt, pepper, oregano, etc.). The sauce I used didn't need any of that, but every sauce is different.

Set sauce on low temp, and get pasta water up to boiling... then start cooking it to box instructions, laying out noodles on wax paper (or silicone) lined pan. You don't have to do them all at once, but instead, some during the actual layering.
Meanwhile, finely chop basil, then mix with ricotta, and parmesan. Salt and pepper optional.
Coarse grate mozzarella cheese.

Steam, or lightly saute the spinach with salt and olive oil. I took the stems off of mine, but leave them if you'd like. The key here is NOT to make it look like fully-cooked collard greens. You want to be able to separate and place the full leaves easily.
Grease a 9x13 glass baking dish (edges included) with olive oil, and then lay down a thin layer of sauce.
Now just start layering the lasagna. Noodles. Ricotta mixture. Sauce. Spinach. Mozzarella. Repeat… Basically until you run out of room or ingredients (preferrably uniform layers).
If refrigerating overnight, wrap with a cling wrap first.
Preheat oven to 375°F
Remove cling wrap from lasagna if having refrigerated overnight, and now cover well with aluminum foil.
First bake for about 50-60 minutes if refrigerated. I don't know for how long if not refrigerated, but I might guess 30 minutes. The key is to get an internal temp of about 155°F.

Remove foil, and let bake in the oven uncovered for another 10-20 minutes until cheese looks at least close to uniformly melted throughout the top layer. If there are exposed pasta edges, they'll start to look a bit crisp.
While cooking the second bake, get 1/2 of the other jar of marinara heated in a sauce pan on the stove. (Store the last 1/2 of that jar in the fridge)
Finally, turn the oven to broil, and cook until top cheese forms spots of golden brown throughout.
After removing from oven, let sit for about 20-30 minutes for more easily removing slices from dish.
To plate, first spread the heated marinara before laying the lasagna slice on top. Optionally, garnish with fresh basil leaves.

recipe.howToTip: Some of these baking times can vary. Once the house starts smelling good, you’re about done with your first bake. The second bake is kind of an “eyeball it” process.

recipe.description: I used a one pot to make this recipe. If you do not have a pressure cooker, you can braise this recipe in the oven slow and low. Instructions will be in notes. #CookPadApron2026
recipe.keywords: smoked pork belly, maple bourbon glaze, slow-cooked pork

recipeInstructions.text: Wash, rinse, and pat dry pork belly. Coat both sides liberally with McCormick brand brown sugar bourbon seasoning. Place into a preheated smoker. Smoke for 1 hour. I smoked at around 165 degrees F. I used hickory wood. After 1 hour, remove pork belly and cut into 1 inch squares.

In your pressure cooker, add apple juice and oil. Add cubed pork belly. Close lid and pressure cook on high for around 30 minutes. There will be extra time to heat up and cool down pressure cooker. When done cooking, let pressure gradually release.

Meanwhile preheat oven to 400 degrees F. In 2 separate bowls, mix dry ingredients for cornbread in one and wet ingredients in another. Mix well. Combine together and fold in. Not to over mix. Place in an 8x8 greased baking dish. Even out and bake on middle rack for 35-40 minutes. It will be well browned when done.
Prepare Brad's collard greens recipe.

Also, right after pressure cooker starts, add all glaze ingredients into a large saucepot. Bring to a simmer. Simmer until sauce thickens over low heat. When pork belly is finished, immediately add to pot with glaze. Minus the braising liquid, discard that. Stir well to coat and continue to cook on low until sauce glazes pork belly. Remove from heat and let cool 5 minutes.
Immediately serve with cornbread and collard greens. Enjoy.

recipe.howToTip:
For the cornbread,  I used cream and water because it makes it drier and more crumbly. If you want a moist bread, use 1 cup milk instead of cream and water. 

If you do not have a pressure cooker, place smoked pork belly, double the apple juice and oil. Place in a covered roasting pan and roast in oven at 325 degrees for 3 to 4 hours. Or until tender. Mix hourly. Then move to the thickened glaze without the braising liquid.
recipeIngredient: 2 tbs McCormick brand brown sugar bourbon seasoning

recipe.name: Sweet and Sour Pork
recipe.description: Sweet and sour pork that adults and children love
recipe.keywords: easy pork recipe, tangy sauce, homemade dinner

recipeInstructions.text:
Marinade:
1 tbsp light soy sauce
1 tsp oyster sauce
A pinch of white pepper
1/4 tsp salt
1 tsp sugar
1 egg
2 tbsp cornstarch

Coating:
100g cornstarch
50g flour
1 tsp baking powder (optional, for a crispier texture)
Sauce

Mix well and set aside:

4 tablespoons tomato sauce

3 tablespoons white vinegar

3 tablespoons sugar

1 tablespoon light soy sauce

100 ml water

1 tablespoon cornstarch (mix with 2 tablespoons water to make a thickening agent)

Preparation Steps

Step 1: Marinating the Pork
Cut the pork into pieces about 3 cm in size.

Add all the marinade ingredients.

Mix well.

Marinate for 20-30 minutes.

Step 2: Frying the Meat
Coat the meat pieces evenly with flour.

Oil temperature approximately 170℃.

Fry for 4-5 minutes until cooked through.

Remove and let rest for 3 minutes.

Increase the oil temperature to 190℃ and fry again for 1 minute.

The result will be:

Crispy outer skin
Juicy meat

Step 3: Stir-fry the side dishes

Leave a small amount of oil in the pan.

Stir-fry in the following order:

Onion, green bell pepper, red bell pepper, pineapple

Stir-fry for about 1 minute.

Step 4: Making the Sauce

Pour in the prepared sauce.

After bringing to a simmer:

Add cornstarch slurry.

Cook until:

The sauce is thickened and glossy.

Step 5: Mix well

Pour in the fried pork.

Stir-fry quickly for about 20-30 seconds, ensuring each piece of meat is evenly coated with the sauce.

Do not overcook, otherwise the outer skin will become soft.

recipe.howToTip:
✅ Made with pork shoulder, which is more tender and flavorful than pork tenderloin.

✅ Double-fried for an extra crispy exterior that doesn't easily become soggy.

✅ Tossed with the sauce last to maintain a crispy exterior and tender interior.

✅ The sweet and sour ratio can be adjusted to taste:

For a sweeter flavor: Increase sugar to 4 tablespoons.

For a more sour flavor: Increase white vinegar to 4 tablespoons.

recipe.name: Marx Meal Prep Stir-Fry (Reduced Sodium)
recipe.description: This is my go to high inside fastball meal prep chicken stirfry, I get a great dinner and 3 great portion lunches out of it for the following few days. I have refined this recipe for months and eat it WEEKLY.
recipe.keywords: healthy stir-fry, reduced sodium recipe, easy meal prep

recipeInstructions.text: Cube up your chicken breast and pan fry in 2 tbsp oil until just cooked. You can hit it with some black pepper (NO SALT). I use a giant wok for cooking everything because, well, you need the room. Once it's cooked, pour it and oil of into a bowl and keep on the side. 5-6 minutes.
Now's a good time to start your white rice in your rice cooker (get a rice cooker if you don't have one). Three scoops rice, three scoops water. Make sure you rinse it first! Plug and play!

Dice up your peppers and onions and sear on low/medium heat in the other 2 tbsp oil until they start to get cooked, don't char or overly cook them though, you still want a bit of snap. You can introduce your minced garlic, minced ginger, black pepper and other seasonings to taste (I usually do a bit extra onion/garlic powder, and a TINY fleck of salt). 5 minutes.
Dump your broccoli florets and peas/carrots in. Mix it all up. I usually add a bit of water here, ~1/4 cup, stir, cover the wok and let this cook awhile (~7-10 minutes) and prep your sauce.

In a bowl or big measuring cup, add in coconut aminos, worcestershire sauce, honey, sriracha, and red pepper flakes. Add your corn starch to 1/2 cup of water and stir with a fork or whisk until you get a slurry, then mix in with the sauce base and stir it up good.

Back to the stir-fry, keep it hot and stirring, dump your bowl of chicken in, and your sauce, and get it all incorporated. Crank the heat to medium/high and keep stirring (you're more or less done an waiting for rice now).

This whole mixture should cook about 10-12 minutes. You want the frozen broccoli cooked and the sauce to gel a bit/thicken. Keep an eye on it and don't let it over cook though, just stir it up good every few minutes. It should have a good amount of sauce in there, with lots of veg submerged, but if you don't see enough for your tastes, add some water.

When your rice is done and your stir-fry well cooked you're set! I usually get a big mixing bowl and dump the rice and all the stir-fry in. Mix it all up then dish it out. I get 3 meal prepped lunch bowls and a decent sized bowl for my dinner, but you can experiment with portion sizes. This keeps in a cold fridge well for up to 4 days.

Included is a snapshot of the nutrients for a 1/4th portion. Yes the sodium is a bit high if you're on a low sodium diet, adjust your other intake accordingly, however, these bowls are super filling and delicious.

recipe.name: Columbia River Salmon Cakes
recipe.description: These Columbia River Salmon Cakes are pure Pacific Northwest comfort with a little Southern fish-fry soul tucked inside. Roasted salmon gets folded with sautéed peppers, onion, celery, capers, parsley, Dijon, mayo, breadcrumbs, and just enough seasoning to make every bite rich, bright, savory, and deeply satisfying. They’re crisp on the outside, tender in the middle, and built to be served the right way: over a big helping of yellow rice with homemade tartar sauce on the side. This is the kind of dish that makes the table go quiet for a minute, which is usually the highest compliment a recipe can earn. One important note: this is not a throw-it-together weeknight dinner. These salmon cakes take time, chilling, cooling, shaping, and a little TLC. But when you finally take that first bite, you’ll know exactly why the extra effort was worth it.
recipe.keywords: salmon patties, seafood recipe, easy dinner

recipeInstructions.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees.

Rinse and pat your salmon fillet dry, then place it skin-side down on a sheet pan lined with tin foil. Baste with olive oil and add salt and black pepper. Roast the salmon for 15 minutes. Remove from the oven and let cool. Once cool enough to handle, wrap the fillet in tin foil and refrigerate. Let it cool for 1-3 hours.
While the salmon is cooking, it's time to get your chop on. Chop your yellow and orange bell peppers, red onion, celery stalks, and mince the parsley. Drain and measure the capers.

Melt 4 tbs. butter in a frying pan (I prefer cast iron), then add 4 tbs. olive oil over medium-high heat. Once hot, add your chopped vegetables, capers, and parsley. Then add Worcestershire, crab boil, and remaining salt and pepper. If you are adding hot sauce, add it now. Once combined, turn the heat to medium-low and stir every few minutes. Cook until vegetables soften, normally about 20 minutes. Once done, pour the contents onto a sheet pan and let cool. Then pour into a bowl and refrigerate.

Once everything has cooled (1-3 hours), add the eggs, Dijon mustard, and mayo to a large mixing bowl. Whisk together till well combined. Then add the vegetable mix and flake the salmon fillet into the bowl (a great time to remove those pesky bones). Finally, add the breadcrumbs and stir until well combined and easy to form into cakes by hand. Chill this for 20-30 minutes in the refrigerator. Shape the cakes by hand into 4 oz. portions and place on parchment paper.

In a large frying pan (again, I prefer cast iron), melt 2 tbs. butter and 2 tbs. olive oil. When hot, add 2-3 cakes to the pan and cook 3-4 minutes per side. Don't crowd the pan. Move cooked cakes to a wire rack over a paper bag to soak up excess oil. Add 2 tbs. and 2 tbs. of olive oil to the pan and repeat the cooking process. Repeat until all the cakes are cooked.

Serve immediately and watch the room go silent with pure flavor joy. I like to serve mine salmon cakes over Caribbean yellow rice and with homemade tartar sauce. Check out the recipes on my profile for these two, if you don't already have your own recipe.

recipe.name: High protein chickpea brownies, vegan and gluten-free
recipe.description: Fudgy chocolate brownies with no flour, no sugar and no whey. The whole thing is built on a can of chickpeas and the liquid it comes in. Aquafaba, the bean water most people pour down the drain, whips up like egg white and gives these their lift. Chia gel does the binding. Dark, dense and properly fudgy, about 95 calories a brownie. Studio Shoki, recipe 02. The art of protein.
recipe.keywords: vegan brownies, gluten-free dessert, high protein snacks

recipeInstructions.text: Stir the chia powder into 60 g of water and leave it 10 to 15 minutes until it thickens to a gel. This is the binder that replaces the egg and the flour.
Whip the aquafaba with an electric mixer for 5 to 8 minutes, until it holds soft peaks. It doesn't need to be meringue-stiff, just light and foamy.
Blend the chickpeas, cocoa, peanut powder, vanilla, salt and the chia gel until completely smooth with no grain left. If it's too thick to move, add water a tablespoon at a time.
Fold the whipped aquafaba into the batter gently with a spatula. Don't stir it flat, the air you just whipped in is what keeps these from being a dense paste.
Spread into a lined 20 x 20 cm pan and bake at 175°C / 350°F for 22 to 28 minutes. Pull it while the centre still looks slightly underdone, it firms as it cools.
Cool completely before slicing, and chill it a few hours if you can. The texture turns properly fudgy in the fridge. Cut into 9.

recipeIngredient: 400 g cooked chickpeas, drained (save the liquid)
100 ml aquafaba (the liquid from the can)
